axelrod1981.title: Cell-substrate contacts illuminated by total internal reflection fluorescence
axelrod1981.use: the evanescent wave I = I0 exp(-z/d) and its decay depth d = lambda / (4 pi n2) (sin^2 theta / sin^2 theta_c - 1)^(-1/2) (eq. 1, 2), i.e. lambda / (4 pi n_s sqrt(u^2 - 1)) with the BFP position u; d diverges at the critical angle; the check value theta = 72.5 deg, n1 = 1.44, theta_c = 67.5 deg, 514.5 nm: d = 120 nm (Fig. 2, Methods)
axelrod1981.checked: equations, the check value and the statements read from the Europe PMC full text (PMC2111781)

axelrod2001.title: Total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy in cell biology
axelrod2001.use: objective-type TIRF through a high-NA objective; the evanescent intensities at the interface for s and p polarisation, I_s(0) = 4 cos^2 theta / (1 - n^2), I_p(0) = 4 cos^2 theta (2 sin^2 theta - n^2) / (n^4 cos^2 theta + sin^2 theta - n^2), n = n2 / n1 (relative to the incident intensity): 4 and 4 / n^2 at the critical angle
axelrod2001.checked: citation and abstract via PubMed (not open access); the intensity formulas are the standard Fresnel results, checked for continuity with the transmitted Fresnel coefficients at the critical angle, not read from this paper's full text

tokunaga2008.title: Highly inclined thin illumination enables clear single-molecule imaging in cells

The sheet geometry here (thickness = beam FWHM / (tan theta_s cos theta_i) on the axis) is derived, not taken from the paper

bornwolf1999.title: Principles of Optics, 7th edition
bornwolf1999.use: Fresnel amplitude transmission coefficients t_s = 2 n1 cos theta_i / (n1 cos theta_i + n2 cos theta_t), t_p = 2 n1 cos theta_i / (n2 cos theta_i + n1 cos theta_t) (section 1.5.2); the power transmittance T = (n2 cos theta_t / n1 cos theta_i) |t|^2 (section 1.5.3: the free imager's collected light into the coverslip, excitation.js collectionRings); Snell's law; the sine condition (the BFP radius ~ n sin theta)
